info.bio: Karlheinz Stockhausen (* 22 de agosto de 1928 en Kerpen-Mödrath, cerca de Colonia, Alemania - 5 de diciembre de 2007) fue uno de los compositores más importantes de música docta del siglo XX. Estudió piano y pedagogía musical en el Conservatorio Superior de Colonia, así como musicología, germanística y filosofía en la universidad de la misma ciudad, dedicándose a la composición desde los años 50 y orientándose desde un principio hacia la música serial. Obras de este período son, entre otras, Kreuzspiel y Formel.

podcast.title: Electronic Music Studio in Cologne (1953)
podcast.body: By 1953, Carlheinz Stockhausen had established an electronic music studio near Cologne, West Germany, which became a focal point for the development of an avant-garde scene experimenting with oscillators, wave generators, tape loops, and white noise composition. "By 1953, Carl Heinstochhausen had an electronic music studio near Cologne, and a little avant-garde scene began to develop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Father of Electronic Music
podcast.body: Stockhausen is recognized as a highly influential German composer and one of the most important experimental musicians of the 20th century, especially for his pioneering work in electronic music. His radical approach in the 1960s was a significant inspiration for young German musicians. "In fact, he has been called the father of electronic music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Can's Atonal Spirit
podcast.body: Can's music, particularly evidenced in tracks like "Aumgn" from "Tago Mago," demonstrated a return to the atonal spirit that was characteristic of Stockhausen's avant-garde compositions. "Temas que les hacía volver al espíritu atonal de Stockhausen."

srcs.episode: CAN ｜ La Banda que (posiblemente) Inspiró a tu banda preferida

podcast.title: Teacher of Can Members
podcast.body: Karlheinz Stockhausen, a prominent figure in contemporary classical and avant-garde music, was the teacher of both Irmin Schmidt and Holger Czukay, two founding members of Can. "un antiguo alumno alemán de Stochhaus en llamado Irmell Smith ... El Jolgue Chukai, otro alumno de Stockhausen"
